Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our standard DPA (v1.0) and the current subprocessor register export.

Quick answers up front:
- DPA: attached (Word + PDF). We typically ask customers to review and propose redlines; we aim to keep data controller/processor roles standard.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV has current entries. Most infra processing occurs in GCP (us-central) with replicas in eu-west for customers who choose EU-only hosting.
- Transfers: Redwood uses the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (EU SCCs 2021) as our primary mechanism. For customers requiring execution, we provide a SCC addendum and can counter-sign. We also offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) if Acme requires an EU-only footprint.

We prefer DocuSign for execution as it preserves the metadata we track in our contract system, but AdobeSign is OK if your legal ops require it — just let us know.

Action items:
- Priya: confirm whether Acme wants SCC addendum executed or an EU-hosting/Private deployment.
- CCing Laura (Head of Privacy Ops) who will ingest redlines and coordinate subprocessor updates.

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-v1.0.docx; Redwood-DPA-v1.0.pdf; Redwood-Subprocessors-2026-03.csv

Hi Priya, Sean — looping in legal to propose a lightweight path to execution. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Scope and roles
- Redwood acts as processor for requests to hosted inference and embeddings. If Acme subscribes to Redwood Private and hosts the runtime, the relationship is controller-to-controller for that environment.

2) Subprocessor detail
- The attached CSV lists our current subprocessors and primary processing region. If Acme needs a contractor-level attestation, we can provide SOC2 reports under NDA.

3) Transfers & execution path
- We use EU SCCs (2021), sign a mutual addendum (we insert Redwood as data processor signatory), and then execute via DocuSign link that seeds into our contract workflow.
- If Acme prefers AdobeSign, we can accommodate but may need to provision a manual import which can add ~24–48 hrs to processing.

4) Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
- Today: Acme confirms preferred execution mechanism and raises any material DPA redlines (high level).
- Wed: Redwood legal to issue a tracked Word with our suggested responses.
- Thu/Fri: Finalize and execute SCC addendum via DocuSign (or AdobeSign if requested).

If you can send the top 3 clauses you want changed, I can prioritize.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks Rishi — that timeline works. Top 3 items from Acme legal:
1) Liability cap clarification for processor acts (we'd like confirmation that caps apply per event and carve outs for wilful misconduct remain).
2) Audit rights & subprocessor notification timing (we prefer 30 days notice for new subprocessor additions).
3) Residuals clause — please confirm no effort to use our data for model training without explicit consent.

We'd prefer AdobeSign for execution (legal ops constraint). If that adds a day or two, that's fine, but please confirm you can import the executed PDF into your contract system.

If you can return a redlined Word by EOD Wed (your Thu), we can get procurement and IT to review. Also requesting a copy of the SOC2 report under NDA — happy to execute an NDA if required.

Attachments: none in this reply.

Best,
Priya
